newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures extend gains in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures extend gains in late trading.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures strengthened further late Friday, with October breaking through resistance on the heels of a strong cash market, industry sources said.
At 1435 EDT, October was up 6.1 cents at $1.870 per million British thermal units after hitting a high of $1.88. November also extended its gains by rising 5.6 cents to $2.045.
"It's purely cash-driven," said one trader, adding that a rally in front of the weekend was fairly bullish for the market.
Technically, October support was seen around the contract low of $1.73 and then at $1.68. Resistance was pegged first in the low-$1.90s, then $1.955.

Cash prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes were talked in the low-to-mid $1.70s, while Midcontinent prices hovered in the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s. The Chicago city-gate market was quoted in the high-$1.70s.
At 1405 EDT, NYMEX said 15,024 Henry Hub contracts traded.
NYMEX's October Permian contract was offered at $1.56, six cents higher than Thursday's settlement.

On the KCBT, October also stretched its lead this afternoon by rising six cents to $1.635. Other front months were two to five cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.5 cents to 22.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
